lines.quote: designed the digital beamforming architecture for Polaris RF Labs' 32-channel coherent receive array, including per-channel gain/phase equalisation, sum-and-delay beam steering, and sidelobe-control weighting

the beamforming system I designed for Polaris's latest 32-channel receiver is the piece of engineering I am most proud of: per-channel equalisation, adaptive sidelobe control, and sum-and-delay beam steering, all running in real time on a single Zynq SoC.

Designed and implemented the embedded digital signal processing firmware in C++ for the PRF-440 digital receiver module, running on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ SoC under hard real-time constraints (8 ms processing window per pulse repetition interval, zero-copy DMA transfers, deterministic memory management).

Developed and maintain the production Python calibration and regression-test framework (pytest-based, approximately 12,000 lines of code) used by the hardware verification team across 14 automated test stations.

Characterised the receive chain's gain flatness and group delay across the 1.27 GHz bandwidth using a Keysight PNA-X network analyser, feeding the resulting calibration tables into the processor's range-matched filter.
M.Sc. Electrical Engineering, Charles River Institute of Technology (CRIT), 2018
